objectives: Derive softmax and explain the temperature knob
Explain why logits are shifted for numerical stability

slides.title: Part 1 — From scores to a decision
slides.body: Every time a neural network *chooses* — the next word, the predicted class, which token to attend to — softmax is the function doing the choosing. Master this one function and three later topics (attention, the output head, temperature sampling) become almost free.

slides.title: The problem softmax solves
slides.body:
A network's final layer outputs **logits** — raw real numbers with no constraints, e.g. `[2.5, 2.0, 1.5, 0.8, 0.3]`. They can be negative; they don't sum to anything in particular. To *act* on them as a choice, we need a **probability distribution**: all values ≥ 0, summing to exactly 1.

Softmax is the standard map from logits to a distribution:

$$\sigma(z)_i = \frac{e^{z_i}}{\sum_j e^{z_j}}$$

The exponential guarantees positivity (even for negative logits); dividing by the sum guarantees normalization. The bars on the right show softmax applied to a fixed logit set — the tallest logit gets the most probability, but not *all* of it.

slides.title: Why not just normalize?
slides.body:
A tempting shortcut: divide each logit by the sum. Two reasons it fails:

1. **Sign.** Logits can be negative; probabilities cannot. `z / Σz` can produce negative or undefined values. $e^{z}$ is always positive.
2. **Contrast.** The exponential is monotonic *and* convex — it stretches gaps. A logit lead of `0.5` becomes a much larger probability lead than linear normalization would give. That controllable contrast is exactly what we exploit next with temperature.

Softmax is also differentiable everywhere, with a clean Jacobian — essential for training by backpropagation.

slides.title: Part 2 — Temperature: one knob, total control
Dividing by T before the exponential
slides.body:
Insert a single scalar **temperature** $T$ before softmax:

$$\sigma(z/T)_i = \frac{e^{z_i/T}}{\sum_j e^{z_j/T}}$$

- **$T < 1$ (cold):** logits are amplified, the gap widens, the distribution becomes **peaked** — the model gets *confident*.
- **$T = 1$:** plain softmax.
- **$T > 1$ (hot):** logits shrink toward each other, the distribution **flattens** toward uniform — the model gets *exploratory*.

The viz now shows a **cold** distribution ($T = 0.5$). Compare its sharpness to the $T = 1$ slide above.

slides.title: The hot regime
slides.body:
Now the **hot** regime ($T = 2$). The same logits, but the bars are far more even — the model is much less sure, and sampling from this distribution produces more varied (and riskier) tokens.

This is *the* generation knob. Greedy decoding is the $T \to 0$ limit (argmax). Creative writing settings push $T$ up. Nothing about the network changes — only this one division.

question.question: Drag the temperature T until the softmax distribution is approximately uniform across all five logits.
question.explanation: As T grows, every z_i / T → 0, so e^(z_i/T) → 1 for all i, and softmax → 1/N uniformly. Large T erases the information in the logits — useful for exploration, fatal for accuracy.

question.question: You want greedy generation (always emit the single highest-probability token). Which temperature regime matches that behavior?
options: T → 0 — softmax sharpens to one-hot on the largest logit (argmax)
T → ∞ — softmax flattens so the top token dominates
T = 1 — the default already is argmax
question.explanation: As T → 0⁺, the largest logit's exponential dominates all others infinitely, so softmax → a one-hot vector on the argmax. Greedy decoding is literally the zero-temperature limit of sampling.

slides.title: Part 3 — Numerical reality + where it reappears
slides.body: Two things every practitioner must know: softmax is computed in a numerically stable way, and it is the same function in three very different places.

slides.title: The max-subtraction trick
slides.body:
Naively, $e^{z_i}$ overflows for large logits (e.g. $e^{1000}$ is `inf`). Every real implementation subtracts the max first:

$$\sigma(z)_i = \frac{e^{z_i - \max_j z_j}}{\sum_k e^{z_k - \max_j z_j}}$$

This is **mathematically identical** (the constant $e^{-\max}$ cancels top and bottom) but numerically safe — the largest exponent is now $e^0 = 1$. If you ever implement softmax from scratch and see `NaN`s, this is almost always why.

question.question: Subtracting max(z) from every logit before exponentiating changes the output probabilities how?
options: Not at all — it is exactly equal, just numerically stable
It only matters when logits are negative
question.explanation: Multiplying numerator and denominator by the same constant e^(−max) leaves the ratio unchanged: softmax is shift-invariant in its input. The trick is purely about avoiding overflow — the distribution is identical.

question.question: Derive softmax
question.goal: From: turn a logit vector z into a probability distribution that is differentiable and monotonic in z.

steps.prompt: We need outputs ≥0 summing to 1, monotonic in z. Which mapping?
steps.motivation: exp is positive, monotone, and turns logit *differences* into probability *ratios* — the property a classifier wants.
hints: Must stay positive and differentiable everywhere.
steps.reveal: exp(z) is positive & monotone; dividing by the sum makes it a distribution.

steps.motivation: Normalizing exp by its sum is the unique map giving a simplex point whose log-odds are linear in z.
hints: Numerator exp(z_i); denominator sums over all classes.

question.question: Crank the temperature up until the distribution's entropy is ≥ 1.0 nats (it flattens toward uniform).
question.harnessCode:
import numpy as np
z=np.array([2.0,1.0,0.1,-0.5,-1.0])
p=np.exp(z/float(T)); p=p/p.sum()
ent=float(-(p*np.log(p+1e-12)).sum())
metrics={'entropy':ent}
question.explanation: High T flattens softmax → high entropy (uncertain); low T sharpens it toward one-hot. Temperature is the confidence knob.

question.prompt: Explain softmax to your pet: why exp, why divide by the sum, and what temperature changes.

rubricCriteria.description: exp keeps values positive and monotonic in the logits
dividing by the sum makes the outputs a probability distribution (sums to 1)
temperature controls how sharp vs. uniform the distribution is

slides.title: What to carry forward
slides.body:
- Softmax turns unconstrained **logits** into a **probability distribution** via $e^{z_i}/\sum e^{z_j}$.
- **Temperature** is a single division that interpolates from argmax ($T\to0$) to uniform ($T\to\infty$).
- It is **shift-invariant**; real code subtracts the max for numerical stability.

You will meet it again as: **[attention](/wiki/attention) weights** (softmax over query·key scores), the **output head** (softmax over vocabulary logits), and **classification**. Same function, three jobs.

**Next:** [Attention](/wiki/attention) — where softmax decides how much each token listens to every other.
